### Selectted Definitions for Reason for Repair

| MAINTENANCE                 |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
|-----------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Breakdown                   | Any failure directly attributable to the equipment that results<br>in the unit being unavailable for operations and requiring<br>either maintenance or repairs to put back into service.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Consumption, Fuel           | Repairs or adjustments required as a result of reviewing fuel consumption records.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Consumption, Oil            | Repairs or adjustments required as a result of reviewing oil consumption records                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Driver's Report             | Any inspection, repairs or adjustments required or performed resulting from a users equipment condition report.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Inspection, Routine         | All normal inspections performed, excluding preventive main-<br>tenance, statutory inspections, or special study of an equip-<br>ments condition.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| Lubrication, Other          | All lubrication not performed as part of a regular preventive maintenance program.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Pre-Delivery                | The inspection, adjustments and repairs required for a new piece of equipment prior to it being placed into service.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Preventive Maintenance (PM) | A program or procedure designed to prevent equipment<br>downtime caused by a component failure. PM procedures in-<br>clude inspections, tests, adjustments, additions, or applications<br>of fluids, gases, and lubricants; cleaning and replacing of filters<br>and emission control devices. PM does not include "repairs."<br>All maintenance, repairs, and parts replacement, except as de-<br>tailed above, performed as the result of PM should be charged<br>to the appropriate vehicle system(s), not to PM. Specific func-<br>tions performed under PM procedures are determined by fleet<br>management and/or manufacturers. |
| Rework                      | The same work performed to correct work improperly per-<br>formed on a previous occasion.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Road Call                   | Any time a mechanic and/or equipment is dispatched to a site<br>away from a company's maintenance facility to either repair<br>or move equipment; or to move it to a location where it can be<br>repaired. These services may be provided in-house or out-<br>sourced.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| Routine                     | The equipment maintenance performed as a result of an in-<br>spection (routine or PM) or scheduled event which returns the<br>equipment to a specified operating condition.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| MANAGEMENT DECISION REPA    | AIRS                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |

### Capital Improvement Vehicle rehabilitation such that the costs incurred are capitalized and would normally be depreciated on the company's books. Conversion A change in the basic configuration of the piece of equipment. This would include such an item as converting a tractor into a tow truck. Modification The alteration of equipment without altering its basic characteristics. Lengthening the frame of a piece of equipment would fall into this classification.

### Special Study

Work resulting from a special examination or inspection of equipment so that a decision can be made, based upon a known set of conditions. This study would normally occur when management is attempting to determine whether or not certain maintenance expenditures should be made relative to a piece of equipment or when a special study is being performed for a manufacturer.

#### **REPAIRS CAUSED BY OUTSIDE INFLUENCE**

| Accident, Non-Reported   | An accident which was not reported by the user.                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
|--------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Accident, Reported       | An accident which was reported by the user.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Manufacturer's Recall    | The repairs incurred as the result of a manufacturer's instruc-<br>tions to inspect, change, or modify a piece of equipment.                                                                                                                      |
| Statutory Inspection     | All inspections required by law.                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Statutory Modifications  | All changes to a vehicle required by law.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Theft                    | Repairs due to the willful removal by parties known or un-<br>known.                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Vandalism                | Repairs due to the willful destruction of equipment.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| Warranty                 | Repairs performed for which compensation is anticipated from the manufacturer or vendor.                                                                                                                                                          |
| Natural Causes           | Repairs to equipment made necessary by those occurrences<br>of nature such as floods, landslides, earthquakes, extremes of<br>weather, and/or the effects of wind, sand, rain, hail, snow, ice,<br>electrical storms and fires of natural origin. |
| Abuse, Equipment         | Repairs required from the abuse, willful or not, of equipment by either operator, maintenance or management action.                                                                                                                               |
| Decommissioned/Sold      | Repairs and/or inspection required to decommission equip-<br>ment, or prepare it for sale.                                                                                                                                                        |
| TOWING                   |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Load Shift/Load Transfer | Repairs to equipment made necessary due to shifting or trans-<br>fer of loads during towing operations.                                                                                                                                           |
| Abandonment              | Repairs to equipment made necessary due to abandonment during towing operations.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Driver Out of Hours      | Expenses made necessary due to driver having insufficient remaining hours for hours-of-service regulatory compliance.                                                                                                                             |
| Lockout                  | Expenses made necessary due to vehicle lockout condition due to repairs, maintenance, inspection, etc.                                                                                                                                            |

# **Code Key 16: Repair Priority**

### Description and Purpose

Code Key 16 records the scheduling priority for work to be performed on equipment.

#### Use

Code Key 16 is used when completing VMRS Repair Order forms (Form 6) and VMRS Special Repair Order forms (Form 7).

### Definition of Repair Priority Classes

| Scheduled    |              | Work is planned. In performing the operation neither the other work in the maintenance facility nor fleet operations will be interrupted.                                                                                                                                            |
|--------------|--------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Non-schedule | ed           | Routine of the maintenance facility is interrupted to perform<br>the work at hand. It usually, but not always, indicates that a<br>mechanic was taken off one job and put on this one. It may,<br>however, reflect that planned priorities had to be adjusted to<br>handle the work. |
| Emergency    |              | Fleet operations are disrupted due to maintenance. In many cases, it requires a driver standing by while the repair is made.                                                                                                                                                         |
| Code         | Repair Class |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |

- Scheduled 1 2
- Non-Scheduled

# **Code Key 19: Indirect Labor Activities**

### Description and Purpose

Code Key 19 records indirect labor activities that are not charged against a specific piece of equipment. It is recommended that, whenever appropriate, a repair order be issued for maintenance operations to be charged against a specific piece of equipment, such as washing a trailer, inspecting a tractor, etc.

#### Use

Code Key 19 is used in conjunction with VMRS *Form 10, "*Indirect Labor Time Card." Code Key 19 may be used in as much detail as desired by the equipment manager to record indirect labor activities to the Indirect Labor Time Card regardless of whether the work is performed by direct or indirect labor personnel.

# Code Key 20: Equipment Status Code

### Description

Code Key 20 describes the status or availability of a piece of equipment for service. It consists of a two-digit numeric code. Code Key 20: Equipment Status Code was introduced with the release of VMRS 2000<sup>™</sup> Version 1.03.

**NOTE:** In releases of VMRS that preceded VMRS 2000<sup>™</sup>, Code Key 20 was used to denote an equipment group. In 1997, Code Key 20 was eliminated to accommodate future expansion of the system codes described in Code Key 31, and used in Code Keys 32 and 33. The information once contained in old Code Key 20—Vehicle Component Groups—is now located as a three-digit system code within Code Key 31. For example, X0X=Cab, Climate Control, Instrumentation and Aerodynamic Devices Group; X1X= Chassis Group; X2X=Drivetrain Group, etc.

| Code | Description                                                                  |
|------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| 01   | Active (equipment currently in service)                                      |
| 02   | New Equipment Available For Assignment                                       |
| 12   | Available For Assignment (Used, Awaiting Reassignment)                       |
| 13   | Decommission To Sell                                                         |
| 15   | Owned Equipment—Repairs Not To Exceed \$500.00 Without Approval              |
| 16   | Owned Equipment—Repairs Not To Exceed \$1000.00 Without Approval             |
| 31   | New Equipment Not In Service (On Order)                                      |

# Code Key 21: New & Retread Tire Out-of-Service Conditions

### Description

Code Key 21: New & Retread Tire Out-of-Service Conditions was developed for tire manufacturers as a means of coding out-of-service conditions as determined by manufacturer/laboratory failure analysis. It is not meant to replace related codes identified for use by technicians in Code Key 18: Technician Failure Code, or Code Key 82: Operator Inspection Vehicle Condition Report. Code Key 21 has two codes per condition, a two-character alpha code or an alternative four-digit numeric code. Code Key 21 was introduced with the release of VMRS 2000<sup>TM</sup> Version 1.03.

NOTE: In releases of VMRS that preceded VMRS 2000<sup>™</sup> Version 1.03, Code Key 21 was used redundantly to denote a vehicle group/system. The information once contained in Code Key 21 was assigned to Code Key 31 in 1997.

# Code Key 22: Tire Management Removal Code

### Description

Code Key 22: Tire Management Removal Code was developed for tire manufacturers as a means of coding tire removal for management reasons. Code Key 21 has two codes per condition, a two-character alpha code or an alternative four-digit numeric code. Code Key 21 was introduced with the release of VMRS 2000<sup>TM</sup> Version 1.03.

**NOTE:** In releases of VMRS that preceded VMRS 2000<sup>TM</sup> Version 1.03, Code Key 22 was used redundantly to denote a vehicle group/system. The information once contained in Code Key 22 was assigned to Code Key 31 in 1997.

| Code (Alpha) | Code (Numeric) | Description                                     |
|--------------|----------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| ET           | 1801           | End of Test                                     |
| HA           | 1802           | Handling Complaint                              |
| LO           | 1803           | Lost/No Record                                  |
| MA           | 1804           | Mate Removal                                    |
| RN           | 1805           | Repairs Exceed Fleet Specifications             |
| CE           | 1806           | Casing Age Exceeds Fleet Specifications         |
| NR           | 1807           | Number of Retreads Exceeds Fleet Specifications |

# **Code Key 23: Tire Position Code**

### Description

In 2016, TMC's VMRS Codes Committee determined that Code Key 79—as currently configured—was not ideally suited for denoting tire position. Therefore, TMC created a separate Code Key for tire position entitled Code Key 23: Tire Position Codes.

Code Key 23 generally follows the coding schema of Code Key 79. However, it has been simplified to meet the needs of tire coding. Code Key 23 consists of four data elements:

- Data Element 1 defines axle type.
- Data Element 2 defines axle sequence.
- Data Element 3 defines left, right or center position relative to axle.
- Data Element 4 defines inner, outer or center position relative to axle.

## Data Element 1 — Axle Type

### Code Description

- S Steer
- D Drive
- T Trailer
- C Converter Dolly
- L Lift
- G Tag
- P Pusher
- F Other Free Rolling Axle
- Z Spare

### Data Element 2 — Axle Sequence

Axle sequence is defined in numerical acending order, starting with first axle at the foremost position on the vehicle.

### **Code Description**

- 1 First
- 2 Second
- 3 Third
- etc. etc.

### Data Element 3 — Left/Right Position

#### Code Description

- L Left
- R Right

### Data Element 4 — Inner/Outer/Center Orientation

#### **Code Description**

- l Inner
- O Outer
- C Center

For all data elements, X is used for "not applicable" and "missing information"

### EXAMPLES

Coding Example 1:

Identify the inner dual tire located on the passenger side of the rear-most tandem axle on a 6X4 tractor (six wheels; four driven) Code; D3RI

- D = Drive
- R= Right
- 3 = Third
- I = Inner

Coding Example 2: Identify the tire located on the driver's side of the steer axle on a 6X4 tractor (six wheels;four driven). Code S1LX S = Steer L = Left 1 = First

X = Not applicable

# Code Key 24: Maintenance Status

### Description

In 2016, TMC's VMRS Codes Committee determined that VMRS needed greater flexibility to describe the maintenance status of a part, system, and/or complete vehicle — beyond the current capacity of existing VMRS Code Keys. Therefore, in 2016, the Committee proposed adoption of a separate Code Key for maintenance status entitled Code Key 24: Maintenance Status. It was balloted and approved in 2016 and officially adopted in 2017.

Code Key 24 employs a two-digit numeric code structure consisting of a single data element. There is no logic to the code structure, other than the codes are issued in sequential numeric order beginning with "01.'

| Code | Description             |    |                           |
|------|-------------------------|----|---------------------------|
| 01   | En Route                | 07 | Waiting for Authorization |
| 02   | Arrived                 | 08 | Repair in Progress/       |
| 03   | Checked-In              | 09 | Repair Complete           |
| 04   | Triage                  | 10 | Ready for Delivery        |
| 05   | Diagnostics in Progress | 11 | Delivered                 |
| 06   | Estimating              |    |                           |
|      |                         |    |                           |

# Code Keys 25-30: (Obsolete) Numbers Reserved for Future Use

### Description

Code Keys 23-30, used in previous releases of VMRS prior to 1997, have been obsolete since 1997. Code Keys 23-30 were eliminated to accommodate future expansion of the system codes described in Code Key 31, and used in Code Keys 32 and 33. The information once contained in Code Keys 23-30 was been merged into Code Key 31 in 1997.

Code Keys 23 and 24 were reassigned in 2017. Code Keys 25-30 remain reserved for future expansion of VMRS<sup>TM</sup>.

# Code Key 31: System Codes

### Description and Purpose

VMRS<sup>™</sup> uses a series of three-digit codes that readily and consistently identify specific equipment systems. For example, brakes are identified as a system by code 013. While these codes are the heart of the "common language" of VMRS and are a vital part of the VMRS concept, they are by themselves nothing more than coding conventions designed for use at all levels within the industry, from fleets to mechanics to manufacturers to suppliers of parts. In order to take advantage of the 3rd digit of the SYSTEM level Code (Code Key 31),TMC redefined the VMRS GROUP portion of the SYSTEM CODE in 2003 as follows:

- There are 10 groups within VMRS Code Key 31 (and CK 32, and CK 33 as well):
  - X0X Cab, Climate Control, Instrumentation, & Aerodynamic Devices Group
  - X1X Chassis Group
  - X2X Drivetrain Group
  - X3X Electrical Group
  - X4X Engine / Motor Systems Group
  - X5X Accessories Group
  - X6X Equipment Dependent Attachments
  - X7X Bodies & Vessels Group
  - X8X Heating & Refrigeration Group
  - X9X Bulk Product Transfer Systems Group
- Under this structure, the 2nd digit of the SYSTEM CODE, identifies the GROUP CODE.
- The 1st and 3rd digits vary to permit additional systems within a GROUP.
- Under the old VMRS 2000<sup>™</sup> (versions 1.00-1.02) structure, the 1st & 2nd digits identified the GROUP CODE.
- Under the original VMRS structure (pre-1997), the first digit of the 2-digit SYSTEM CODE identified the GROUP CODE.

This change in convention preserves the traditional definition of GROUPS within systems and is consistently backward compatible with all previous versions of VMRS and VMRS 2000<sup>™</sup>.

#### Use

Use of Code Key 31 is one of the minimum requirements for using VMRS properly, as was described in Chapter 1 of this *Handbook*. For additional levels of coding detail, use the six-digit codes from Code Key 32: Assembly Codes, or the nine-digit codes from Code Key 33: Component Codes.

# **Code Key 32: Assembly Codes**

### Description, Purpose and Use

Through the use of assembly level codes, VMRS provides additional capability to further define Code Key 31's System Codes. The first classification below the system level is referred to as the assembly. At this level, all major groupings within each system are broken out and reported through the use of a three digit code. These, when used with their system prefix, identify the specific assembly within a piece of equipment. For example, front brakes and drums can be identified by a combination of the System and Assembly Code 013-001.

While these codes are the heart of the "common language" of VMRS and are a vital part of the VMRS concept, they are by themselves nothing more than coding conventions designed for use at all levels within the industry—fleets, mechanics, manufacturers, and parts suppliers.

A complete listing of Code Key 32 follows.

# **Code Key 33: Component Codes**

## Description, Purpose and Use

Through the use of component level codes, VMRS provides additional capability to further define Code Key 31's System Codes down to the individual part level. Used together, Code Keys 31-33 define the nine-digit VMRS component code.

| XXX<br>System | XXX<br>Assembly<br>Within System | XXX<br>Level Part Level<br>Within Assembly |
|---------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------------------------|
|               | CODING EXAMPLE                   |                                            |
| 013<br>Brakes | 001<br>Front<br>Brakes and Drums | 015<br>Brake Lining, Front                 |

#### Note

The complete list of all VMRS Code Key 33 Component Codes appears in Appendix III of this *Handbook,* in both alphabetical and numerical order.

# # #

# Code Key 34: Manufacturer/Supplier/Brand Codes

### Description, Purpose and Use

In order not to disturb either the manufacturers' or suppliers' unique numbering system, VMRS<sup>™</sup> uses its own generic means of identifying manufacturers/suppliers and/or brands. The identifier is a five-character alpha code, assigned by TMC, and used as a prefix to the manufacturers', suppliers' and/or brand unique number. It is not the intent of VMRS to supplant the manufacturers'/suppliers'/brand unique part numbering systems, but rather to supplement them.

When a Code Key 34 manufacturer's code and part number are used in conjunction with the VMRS System/Assembly/Component level codes (Code Key 33), precise identification of a specific part is possible on a universal basis. This commonality of identification on a consistent basis is a prerequisite to developing an industry data base for analysis of maintenance information or for mutually exchanging information on a meaningful basis.

A complete listing of Code Key 34 follows. Companies whose names are in ALL CAPS are legacy assignments to VMRS Code Key 34 made prior to 1997.

The five-character alpha manufacturer code is used to complete Equipment Master Records, Repair Orders, etc. An example of the different components of Code Key 34 is shown below:

## **Code Key 36: Power Take Off**

## Description and Purpose

Code Key 36 indicates whether or not a piece of equipment features a Power Take Off (PTO) device.

### Use

Code Key 36 is used with VMRS Equipment Master Record forms. On "Form 1, Equipment Master Record—Power Units," it is entered as the seventh digit of the Transmission Type Code, Line H7, see Instruction Set 2.

| Code | Description       |
|------|-------------------|
| 1    | Power Take Off    |
| 2    | No Power Take Off |

## **Code Key 37: Rear Axle Configuration**

## Description and Purpose

Code Key 37 describes powered rear axle configuration.

#### Use

Code Key 37 is used with VMRS Equipment Master Record forms. On *"Form 1*, Equipment Master Record—Power Units," it is entered as the fourth digit of the Rear Axle Type Code, Line L9, see Instruction Set 4.

| Code | Configuration                          | Abbreviation     |
|------|----------------------------------------|------------------|
| 1    | Single Speed, Single Reduction         | Sgl Spd Sgl      |
| 2    | Single Speed, Double Reduction         | Sgl Spd - Dbl    |
| 3    | Two Speed, Single Reduction            | Two Spd - Sgl    |
| 4    | Two Speed, Double Reduction            | Two Spd - Dbl    |
| 5    | Three Speed, Single Reduction (Tandem) | 3 Spd - Sgl, Tdm |
| 6    | Planetary                              | PIntry           |
| 7    | Three Speed, Double Reduction (Tandem) | 3 Spd - Dbl, Tdm |

# Code Key 52: Part Status Code

### Description and Purpose

Code Key 52 identifies the status of an equipment subsystem, assembly or part. Its primary usages are for comparative maintenance analysis purposes and for inventory control systems.

| <i>Definitions</i><br>New | Not previously having been installed or in use.                                                                             |
|---------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Rebuilt/Remanufactured    | To restore to a previous state by replacement of components, refinishing, rebrushing, or to manufacture into a new product. |
| Used                      | Item has had previous service. May be cleaned and placed in stock, but has not been rebuilt.                                |
| Retreaded, New            | A retreaded tire that has not been in service since retreading.                                                             |
| Retreaded, Used           | A retreaded tire placed in service since retreading.                                                                        |
| Remolding, New            | A remolded tire that has not been in service since remolding.                                                               |
| Remolding, Used           | A remolded tire that has been in service since remolding.                                                                   |
| Repaired                  | Part is brought back to serviceable / operable condition.                                                                   |
| Arrived                   | Part is available for use at the intended location.                                                                         |

| Code | Condition              |
|------|------------------------|
| 1    | New                    |
| 2    | Rebuilt/Remanufactured |
| 3    | Used                   |
| 5    | Retreaded, new         |
| 6    | Retreaded, used        |
| 7    | Remolded, new          |
| 8    | Remolded, used         |
| 9    | Repaired               |
| 10   | Arrived                |

# Code Key 76: Reason for Delay

#### Description and Purpose

Code Key 76 describes the reason for delay in the completion of work on equipment which has entered the maintenance facility. It is entered in the "Delay" column of the Repair Order Log (*Form 20 or 21*). It provides valuable data on maintenance facility operations for subsequent analysis and management action.

| <i>Definition of Terms</i><br>Parts, Out of Stock | Parts normally stocked at the reporting facility.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
|---------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Parts, Not Stocked                                | Parts not normally stocked at the reporting facility and which must either be purchased or transferred to the reporting facility.                                                                                                                 |
| Labor, Not Available                              | At either the company or vendor's facility intended to perform the work.                                                                                                                                                                          |
| Space, Not Available                              | At either the company or vendor facility.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Special Tools Required                            | Tools required to complete work not in facility's normal inventory.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Awaiting Approval                                 | Management approval and authorization required before work can be<br>performed. Unanticipated overhaul, warranty work, insurance adjust-<br>ments, are examples.                                                                                  |
| Other                                             | Delays not appropriate to be identified in the categories above. The spe-<br>cific reason for using "Other" delay" should be identified in the remarks<br>column of the Repair Order Log. Examples include natural causes,<br>power outages, etc. |
| Parts, missing                                    | Parts missing from inventory or parts kit.                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| Technical Support                                 | Awaiting additional technical support to complete repair.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| Waiting for Tow                                   | Unit out-of-service awaiting towing services.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Management Decision                               | Delay prompted by fleet/company management.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Waiting on Warranty Decision                      | Awaiting action on warranty negotiation/determination.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| Weather                                           | Delay caused by inclement weather not conducive to repair completion.                                                                                                                                                                             |

# **Code Key 79: Position Codes**

#### Description and Purpose

Position codes apply where multiples of an identical component performing the same function within the VMRS assembly can be installed on the same unit (equipment).

The following rules apply when assigning a "position" code:

- 1. The equipment configuration at the time the work is performed becomes the determining factor when assigning a "position" code. All position codes are based on the drivers seat perspective. The hierarchy is as follows: Front to rear; Left to right; Top to bottom; Sequential.
- 2. Position codes are a function of the specific VMRS assembly being reported.
- 3. When more than one (1) of the same component exists within the hierarchy of a VMRS assembly, then a sequence code must be used.
- 4. Application of "position" codes follows the schema detailed below.
- 5. Position coding is independent of manufacturer's specific numbering convention (example: engines, transmissions, differentials).
- 6. For engines, transmissions and differentials, side planes are defined by the manufacturer's accepted orientation and are installation independent.

Originally, Code Key 79 was a composite of three subsets or elements: Code Key 79a—Side Code; Code Key 79b—Orientation Code; and Code Key 79c—Sequence Code. The original code schema appears at the bottom of this page.

| Example: | Position Code 02-05-0 |                                 |                          |
|----------|-----------------------|---------------------------------|--------------------------|
| -        | 02=Rear (Side Code)   | 05=Top/Upper (Orientation Code) | 01=First (Sequence Code) |

| Old Co<br>Code | ode Key 79a: Side Code<br>Position | Old Co<br>Code | ode Key 79c: Sequence Code<br>Position |
|----------------|------------------------------------|----------------|----------------------------------------|
| 00             | Not Applicable                     | 00             | Not Applicable                         |
| 01             | Front                              | 01             | First                                  |
| 02             | Rear                               | 02             | Second                                 |
| 03             | Left                               | 03             | Third                                  |
| 04             | Right                              | 04             | Fourth                                 |
| 05             | Top/Upper                          | 05             | Fifth                                  |
| 06             | Bottom/Lower                       | 06             | Sixth                                  |
|                |                                    | 07             | Seventh                                |
| Old Co         | ode Key 79b:Orientation Code       | 08             | Eighth                                 |
| Code           | Position                           | 09             | Ninth                                  |
| 00             | Not Applicable                     | 10             | Tenth                                  |
| 05             | Top/Upper                          | 11             | Eleventh                               |
| 06             | Bottom/Lower                       | and            | so on.                                 |
| 07             | Center                             |                |                                        |
| 08             | Inner                              |                |                                        |
| 09             | Outer                              |                |                                        |

#### New Code Structure

In 2007, TMC's membership approved a restructuring of the coding schema. The updated Code Key 79 defines position through two Code Key subsets or elements: Code Key 79a: Side and Orientation Code and Code Key 79b: Sequence Code.

#### Code Key 79a Side and Orientation Code

This two-digit alpha-numeric code combines the former Side and Orientation elements into one. Codes define the side and orientation (first—front to rear, second—left to right, third—top to bottom; fourth—inner to outer) relative to the driver seat orientation. The code must be considered in conjunction with Code Key 33: Component Code.

#### Code Key 79b Sequence Code

This code remains as originally defined—a numeric, two-digit sequential code. Taken together, these subsets would define position in a four-digit code: Example: 02-01 where

> 02=Front Left 01=Position 1 or First

An alternate code schema is offered for Code Key 79a: Side and Orientation Code which consists of four data elements, each of which is expressed as a alpha character. This schema is easier to remember and visually intuative.

Data Element 1 defines Front or Rear where: F=Front; R=Rear; X= not applicable. Data Element 2 defines Left or Right where: L=Left; R=Right; X= not applicable. Data Element 3 defines Top/Upper or Bottom/Lower where:

T=Top/Upper; B=Bottom/Lower; X=not applicable

Data Element 4 defines Inner, Outer, Center, Inner and Outer and All where: I=Inner; O=Outer; C=Center; E=Inner and Outer; A=All; X=not applicable.

| Example: | F L X X-01          | where |
|----------|---------------------|-------|
| -        | F L X X =Front Left |       |
|          | 01=Position 1 or Fi | irst  |

The sole exception to this schema is the definition of circular, which is expressed as "C C C C".

# Code Key 80: Severity of Service

#### Description and Purpose

Code Key 80 defines severity of service for various types of operations.

| ion |
|-----|
|     |

- 01 Light service, linehaul
- 02 Moderate service, linehaul
- 03 Severe service, linehaul
- 04 Light service, P&D
- 05 Moderate service, P&D
- 06 Severe service, P&D

#### Definitions

#### 01 Light Service, linehaul

- Transportation over long distances in high mileage operations (over 60,000 miles per year.)
- Equipment travels greater than 30 miles between stops.
- Operation on road surfaces of good to excellent concrete or asphalt. (typical)
- Duty is 100 percent load going and 60 percent (or less) load return with grades encountered normally not exceeding eight percent.

#### 02 Moderate Service, linehaul

- Transportation of freight over long distances in high mileage operations (over 60,000 miles per year.)
- Equipment travels greater than 30 miles between stops.
- Operation on road surfaces of good to excellent concrete or asphalt. (typical)
- Duty is loaded full time (more than 60 percent load return) with grades encountered normally not exceeding eight percent.

#### 03 Severe Service, linehaul

- Transportation of freight over long distances in high mileage operations (over 60,000 miles per year.)
- Equipment travels greater than 30 miles between stops.
- Operation on Turnpike only except for loading and unloading at nearby terminals. Road surfaces of good to excellent concrete or asphalt. (typical)
- Duty is loaded full time (more than 60 percent load return) with grades encountered not exceeding three percent.

#### 04 Light Service, pickup and delivery

- Pickup and delivery service within cities and / or suburban areas (short haul, less than 60,000 miles per year).
- Operation on paved road surfaces of concrete or asphalt.
- Grades are defined as light (to about eight percent) which would be typical of geographic areas of operation such as metropolitan Chicago or Detroit.
- Approximately three miles between starts/stops (average). 100 percent load going /40 percent load return (typical).

#### 05 Moderate Service, pickup and delivery

- Pickup and delivery service within cities and / or suburban areas (short haul, less than 60,000 miles per year).
- Operation on paved road surfaces of concrete or asphalt.
- Grades are defined as moderate (to about 12 percent) which would be typical of geographic areas of operation such as metropolitan Atlanta or Seattle.
- Approximately three miles between starts/stops (average). 100 percent load going /40 percent load return (typical).

#### 06 Severe Service, pickup and delivery

- Pickup and delivery service within cities and/or suburban areas (short haul, less than 60,000 miles per year).
- Operation on paved road surfaces of concrete or asphalt.
- Grades are defined as severe (to about 20 percent) which would be typical of geographic areas of operation such as metropolitan Pittsburgh or San Francisco.
- Approximately three miles between starts/stops (average). 100 percent load going /40 percent load return (typical).

Instruction Set 12 (formerly Code Key 69) is a composite of VMRS Code Keys 2, 66, 67, 5, 6, and 68. Taken together, it describes the general characteristics of individual mechanical refrigeration units.

# Appendix IIa: Code Key 32 – Assembly Codes (Alphabetical Order)

#### Description, Purpose and Use

Through the use of assembly level codes, VMRS provides additional capability to further define Code Key 31's System Codes. The first classification below the system level is referred to as the assembly. At this level, all major groupings within each system are broken out and reported through the use of a three digit code. These, when used with their system prefix, identify the specific assembly within a vehicle. For example, front brakes and drums can be identified by a combination of the System and Assembly Code 013-001.

While these codes are the heart of the "common language" of VMRS and are a vital part of the VMRS concept, they are by themselves nothing more than coding conventions designed for use at all levels within the industry—fleets, mechanics, manufacturers, and parts suppliers.

For quick reference, a complete listing of Code Key 32 follows. It also appears within Appendix I of this *Handbook*.
